title: Céline Dion Is Determined To Fight On Amid 17-Year Battle With Stiff-Person Syndrome Ahead of Return to Stage in Paris: ‘I’m Living the Life’
summary: "They paid for tickets. They bought my records. They gave me that luxury," she told Harper's Bazaar about her devoted fans. "So the least I can do is tell them I'm alive."
body: Céline Dion is gearing up for her grand return to the stage with a five-week, 16-show run at Paris’ La Défense Arena this fall slated to kick off on Sept. 12 and run through an Oct. 17 gig, before returning in the spring for another 10 shows in May 2027. But first, the beloved vocal powerhouse is opening up about the devastating 2022 medical diagnosis that nearly derailed her chart-topping career, and life. In an emotional profile in Harper’s Bazaar magazine, Dion, 58, reveals that her battle with the rare neurological disorder Stiff-Person Syndrome was even longer than previously detailed and that despite its debilitating effects, she is determined to fight on. Dion has only performed once in the past six years, delivering an emotional rendition of Édith Piaf’s “Hymne A L’Amour” from the Eiffel Tower at the 2024 Paris Olympics, a one-song performance that proved that she had not lost any of her signature vocal prowess. summary: The first version of Android’s advanced flow is gradually arriving, with a restart and 24-hour delay built in.
body: TL;DR Google has started rolling out Android’s advanced flow for installing apps from unverified developers. The sideloading process includes a restart and a 24-hour wait, while ADB remains exempt from the verification requirement. The rollout comes ahead of developer verification enforcement, which starts September 30 in four countries. Google’s controversial new rules for installing apps from unverified developers are getting very real fast. We first learned in March that Android would introduce a new process for users who still want to sideload those apps, complete with a 24-hour waiting period. Google has now started rolling out that “advanced flow” ahead of the first checkpoint for developer verification. The news comes from Google’s Android Community Engagement Manager Mishaal Rahman (formerly of this parish), who announced the rollout in a post on the r/Android subreddit . Google is calling this the first version of the advanced flow and says it’s rolling out gradually, so you may not see the new setting immediately. The post also fills in several important details about how the system works in practice.

Rumors over the past couple of years have indicated that Apple is working on a version of the AirPods with built-in cameras. Then, in May, these AI-powered earbuds reached a new company milestone , suggesting a launch wasn’t far away. We’re now gaining additional information about what these AirPods can do, while also potentially getting our first look at the earbuds themselves. title: Bizarre YouTube bug is completely wiping out comments and video details, but a fix is coming
summary: Exiting full screen leaves a blank void where comments and titles are meant to be.
body: TL;DR Google has acknowledged a YouTube iPad bug that erases titles, descriptions, and comments when exiting full screen. The bug likely stems from iPad app version 21.32.4 released last week, though Google has not confirmed the trigger. Affected users can temporarily restore missing UI elements by toggling portrait and landscape mode in full screen. Google has officially acknowledged a widespread full-screen bug in the YouTube iPad app that wipes out video titles, descriptions, channel information, and comment sections entirely. A post in the community forum confirmed that engineering teams are actively investigating the flaw and developing a permanent software fix. The bug began surfacing over the weekend as user reports flooded Reddit and Google’s official support forums . When viewers exit full-screen playback on an iPad, the entire interface region below the video player turns blank. Attempting to start a new video fails to fix the broken layout, as the missing UI carries over from one video to the next within the active app session.

It launched the Fairphone Gen 6 last year, and it’s now offering a mid-gen refresh of sorts. This is the Fairphone Gen 6 Plus, and it’s now officially available in the US. However, the Fairphone Gen 6 Plus is officially available in the US via Fairphone.com and Amazon. This device also ships with the standard Google-equipped OS instead of /e/OS, complete with an in-house gallery app for the first time. The official rollout confirms new features, including Bixby troubleshooting, ecosystem device management, and side-by-side repair cost estimates. Samsung is finally giving us a closer look at the Warranty and care feature we first spotted hiding in an early One UI 9 build back in March. In a blog post , the company has detailed how the support hub works, revealing a more comprehensive system for checking warranties, diagnosing problems, comparing repair costs, and getting help without leaving the Settings app. We already knew the basic idea. Our earlier teardown found a work-in-progress Warranty and care tool that appeared to bring warranty information, diagnostics, repairs, and customer support together.
